title: CTS Parables of the Bible — Unit 4: The Plumb Line

blocks.en: 📏 Parables of the Bible — Unit 4: The Plumb Line
blocks.es_reference: 📏 Las Parábolas de la Biblia — Unidad 4: La Plomada

blocks.en: Professor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers
blocks.es_reference: Profesor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers

blocks.en: "Behold, I am setting a plumb line in the midst of My people Israel; I will not pass by them anymore." — Amos 7:8 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "He aquí, yo pongo plomada de albañil en medio de mi pueblo Israel; no lo toleraré más." — Amós 7:8 (RVG)

blocks.en: Orientation
blocks.es_reference: Orientación

blocks.en: My father grew up on a farm, and farmers in those days had to be carpenters too. For a few years he worked as a carpenter to support the family. In our garage there were some very old tools, and one of them was a plumb line made of brass: a weight on the end of a string. A plumb line is about the simplest tool a builder owns, but it does not lie. Gravity pulls the weight straight down, and when you hold the string beside a wall, you know at once whether the wall is straight or leaning.
blocks.es_reference: Mi padre creció en una granja, y en aquellos días los agricultores también tenían que ser carpinteros. Por algunos años trabajó como carpintero para sostener a la familia. En nuestro garaje había herramientas muy viejas, y una de ellas era una plomada de latón: una pesa al final de un hilo. La plomada es quizás la herramienta más sencilla que tiene un constructor, pero no miente. La gravedad jala la pesa directamente hacia abajo, y cuando uno sostiene el hilo junto a una pared, sabe de inmediato si la pared está derecha o inclinada.

blocks.en: In Amos 7:7–9 God showed the prophet Amos a plumb line. It is one of the shortest parables in the Bible, only three verses, but it asks one of the most searching questions a person or a church can face: when God holds His straight standard beside my life, what does He see? In Units 2 and 3 we heard God looking for fruit in His vineyard and shaping clay on His wheel. Now we watch Him measuring a wall.
blocks.es_reference: En Amós 7:7–9 Dios le mostró al profeta Amós una plomada. Es una de las parábolas más cortas de la Biblia, solo tres versículos, pero hace una de las preguntas más penetrantes que una persona o una iglesia puede enfrentar: cuando Dios pone Su norma recta junto a mi vida, ¿qué ve? En las Unidades 2 y 3 vimos a Dios buscando fruto en Su viña y formando barro en Su rueda. Ahora lo vemos midiendo un muro.

blocks.en: I. The Prophet and His Times
blocks.es_reference: I. El profeta y su tiempo

blocks.en: Amos was not a professional prophet. "I was no prophet, nor was I a son of a prophet, but I was a sheepbreeder and a tender of sycamore fruit" (Amos 7:14). He came from Tekoa, a village in Judah south of Bethlehem, but God sent him north to the kingdom of Israel during the reign of Jeroboam II, around 760 BC (Amos 1:1).
blocks.es_reference: Amós no era un profeta de profesión: "No soy profeta, ni soy hijo de profeta, sino que soy boyero, y recojo higos silvestres" (Amós 7:14). Venía de Tecoa, una aldea de Judá al sur de Belén, pero Dios lo envió al norte, al reino de Israel, durante el reinado de Jeroboam II, alrededor del 760 a. C. (Amós 1:1).

blocks.en: Those were boom years. Israel had recovered territory, trade was strong, and the wealthy built summer houses and winter houses decorated with ivory (Amos 3:15). The religious shrines at Bethel and Gilgal were crowded with worshipers. By outward measures Israel looked blessed. But underneath the prosperity the nation was leaning badly. The rich "sell the righteous for silver, and the poor for a pair of sandals" (Amos 2:6). Judges took bribes (5:12). Merchants cheated with false scales (8:5). The wealthy lounged on ivory couches, drank wine by the bowlful, and were "not grieved for the affliction of Joseph" (6:4–6).
blocks.es_reference: Fueron años de bonanza. Israel había recuperado territorio, el comercio era fuerte y los ricos construían casas de verano y casas de invierno decoradas con marfil (Amós 3:15). Los santuarios de Bet-el y Gilgal estaban llenos de adoradores. Por fuera Israel parecía bendecido. Pero debajo de la prosperidad la nación estaba muy inclinada. Los ricos vendían "por dinero al justo, y al pobre por un par de zapatos" (Amós 2:6). Los jueces recibían soborno (5:12). Los comerciantes engañaban con balanzas falsas (8:5). Los ricos se recostaban en camas de marfil, bebían vino en tazones y no se afligían por el quebrantamiento de José (6:4–6).

blocks.en: II. Five Visions (Amos 7–9)
blocks.es_reference: II. Cinco visiones (Amós 7–9)

blocks.en: The plumb line is the third of five visions God gave Amos. In the first, Amos saw locusts devouring the crops. He cried out, "O Lord GOD, forgive, I pray! How shall Jacob stand, for he is small?" and "the LORD relented concerning this" (7:1–3). In the second, he saw a consuming fire, and again he prayed, and again the LORD relented (7:4–6). Here we see the same truth we met in Jeremiah 18: God's announced judgments are real, and He responds to prayer and repentance.
blocks.es_reference: La plomada es la tercera de cinco visiones que Dios dio a Amós. En la primera, Amós vio langostas devorando las cosechas. Clamó: "Señor Jehová, perdona ahora; ¿quién levantará a Jacob? porque es pequeño", y "se arrepintió Jehová de esto" (7:1–3). En la segunda, vio un fuego consumidor, y de nuevo oró, y de nuevo Jehová se arrepintió (7:4–6). Aquí vemos la misma verdad que encontramos en Jeremías 18: los juicios anunciados por Dios son reales, y Él responde a la oración y al arrepentimiento.

blocks.en: But the third vision is different. "Behold, the Lord stood on a wall made with a plumb line, with a plumb line in His hand. And the LORD said to me, 'Amos, what do you see?' And I said, 'A plumb line.' Then the Lord said: 'Behold, I am setting a plumb line in the midst of My people Israel; I will not pass by them anymore'" (7:7–8). This time Amos does not intercede. There is nothing to argue. A plumb line does not debate; it only shows what is true. The wall had been built straight, but it had drifted, and now the Owner was measuring it.
blocks.es_reference: Pero la tercera visión es diferente: "He aquí el Señor estaba sobre un muro hecho a plomo, y en su mano una plomada de albañil. Jehová entonces me dijo: ¿Qué ves tú, Amós? Y dije: Una plomada de albañil. Y el Señor dijo: He aquí, yo pongo plomada de albañil en medio de mi pueblo Israel; no lo toleraré más" (7:7–8). Esta vez Amós no intercede. No hay nada que discutir. La plomada no debate; solo muestra la verdad. El muro se había construido derecho, pero se había desviado, y ahora el Dueño lo estaba midiendo.

blocks.en: Two more visions follow. A basket of summer fruit (8:1–3) contains a Hebrew wordplay: summer fruit is qayits, and the end is qets. Israel was ripe for judgment. In the final vision the Lord stands beside the altar and commands that the temple be struck (9:1). The visions move from judgment averted by prayer to judgment that can no longer be delayed.
blocks.es_reference: Siguen dos visiones más. Un canastillo de fruta de verano (8:1–3) contiene un juego de palabras hebreo: la fruta de verano es qayits, y el fin es qets. Israel estaba maduro para el juicio. En la visión final el Señor está junto al altar y manda que se golpee el templo (9:1). Las visiones pasan del juicio evitado por la oración al juicio que ya no puede demorarse.

blocks.en: A note for careful students: the Hebrew word translated "plumb line," 'anak, appears only here in the Old Testament, and some scholars think it means "tin" or "lead." Most translations still read "plumb line," and the image of a builder's weighted line fits the context of a wall being measured. Whichever meaning is correct, the point of the vision is clear: God was measuring His people and finding them crooked.
blocks.es_reference: Una nota para los estudiantes cuidadosos: la palabra hebrea traducida "plomada", 'anak, aparece solo aquí en el Antiguo Testamento, y algunos eruditos piensan que significa "estaño" o "plomo". La mayoría de las traducciones todavía dicen "plomada", y la imagen de la cuerda con pesa del constructor encaja con el contexto de un muro medido. Sea cual sea el significado correcto, el punto de la visión es claro: Dios estaba midiendo a Su pueblo y lo hallaba torcido.

blocks.en: III. The Plumb Line in Scripture
blocks.es_reference: III. La plomada en la Escritura

blocks.en: Amos was not the only prophet to use the image. Isaiah heard God say, "I will make justice the measuring line, and righteousness the plummet" (Isaiah 28:17). In 2 Kings 21:13 God warned that He would stretch over Jerusalem "the plummet of the house of Ahab," the same standard of judgment that had fallen on the wicked northern dynasty. The plumb line stands for God's own standard of right. It does not change with culture, with wealth, or with popular opinion.
blocks.es_reference: Amós no fue el único profeta que usó la imagen. Isaías oyó a Dios decir: "Y ajustaré el juicio a cordel, y a nivel la justicia" (Isaías 28:17). En 2 Reyes 21:13 Dios advirtió que extendería sobre Jerusalén "la plomada de la casa de Acab", la misma norma de juicio que había caído sobre la malvada dinastía del norte. La plomada representa la norma de justicia de Dios mismo. No cambia con la cultura, con la riqueza ni con la opinión popular.

blocks.en: In the New Testament the standard becomes a Person. Paul speaks of growing up "to the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ" (Ephesians 4:13). Jesus is not only the One who measures; He is the measure. When God holds up His plumb line today, He holds up His Son.
blocks.es_reference: En el Nuevo Testamento la norma se convierte en una Persona. Pablo habla de crecer "a la medida de la estatura de la plenitud de Cristo" (Efesios 4:13). Jesús no solo es el que mide; Él es la medida. Cuando Dios levanta Su plomada hoy, levanta a Su Hijo.

blocks.en: IV. Three Walls Out of Plumb
blocks.es_reference: IV. Tres muros fuera de plomo

blocks.en: The plumb line measured Israel in Amos's day, but it has never been put away. We can hold it beside three groups: Israel then, the religious leaders of Jesus' day, and the church now.
blocks.es_reference: La plomada midió a Israel en los días de Amós, pero nunca ha sido guardada. Podemos ponerla junto a tres grupos: Israel entonces, los líderes religiosos en los días de Jesús y la iglesia ahora.

blocks.en: 1. Israel in Amos's Day
blocks.es_reference: 1. Israel en los días de Amós

blocks.en: Sacrifices without obedience. God said, "I hate, I despise your feast days... Though you offer Me burnt offerings and your grain offerings, I will not accept them" (Amos 5:21–22). The burnt offering, in which the whole animal was burned on the altar, was meant to picture complete surrender to God. Israel kept the ritual and abandoned the surrender. When I was growing up I had a good friend who sometimes spent Saturday night doing things he was not proud of. But on Sunday morning he was faithful to put his tithe in the offering plate, as if he were paying for Saturday night. God does not accept sacrifice in place of obedience.
blocks.es_reference: Sacrificios sin obediencia. Dios dijo: "Aborrecí, abominé vuestras solemnidades... Y si me ofreciereis vuestros holocaustos y vuestras ofrendas, no los recibiré" (Amós 5:21–22). El holocausto, en el que todo el animal se quemaba sobre el altar, debía representar la entrega completa a Dios. Israel guardó el ritual y abandonó la entrega. Cuando yo era joven tenía un buen amigo que a veces pasaba el sábado en la noche haciendo cosas de las que no se sentía orgulloso. Pero el domingo en la mañana era fiel en poner su diezmo en el plato de la ofrenda, como si estuviera pagando por el sábado. Dios no acepta el sacrificio en lugar de la obediencia.

blocks.en: Religion without justice. The poor could not get a fair hearing. The courts were bought, the scales were rigged, and a person could be sold into slavery over a debt as small as the price of a pair of sandals. So God said, "Let justice run down like water, and righteousness like a mighty stream" (Amos 5:24). The prophet Micah summed it up in a single verse: "He has shown you, O man, what is good; and what does the LORD require of you but to do justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God?" (Micah 6:8).
blocks.es_reference: Religión sin justicia. El pobre no podía obtener una audiencia justa. Los tribunales estaban comprados, las balanzas estaban alteradas, y una persona podía ser vendida como esclava por una deuda tan pequeña como el precio de un par de sandalias. Por eso Dios dijo: "Pero corra el juicio como las aguas, y la justicia como impetuoso arroyo" (Amós 5:24). El profeta Miqueas lo resumió en un solo versículo: "Oh hombre, él te ha declarado lo que es bueno, y qué pide Jehová de ti: solamente hacer justicia, y amar misericordia, y humillarte ante tu Dios" (Miqueas 6:8).

blocks.en: A builder who ignores a small lean early in construction will see the whole building fall later. Israel ignored the plumb line, and in 722 BC the northern kingdom fell to Assyria. Its people were scattered, and the nation of Israel in the north never returned.
blocks.es_reference: El constructor que ignora una pequeña inclinación al principio de la obra verá caer todo el edificio después. Israel ignoró la plomada, y en el 722 a. C. el reino del norte cayó ante Asiria. Su pueblo fue esparcido, y la nación de Israel en el norte nunca regresó.

blocks.en: 2. The Jewish Leaders in Jesus' Day
blocks.es_reference: 2. Los líderes judíos en los días de Jesús

blocks.en: Seven centuries later, after exile and return, the people of God no longer bowed to carved idols. But the wall was still leaning in other ways.
blocks.es_reference: Siete siglos después, tras el exilio y el regreso, el pueblo de Dios ya no se inclinaba ante ídolos tallados. Pero el muro seguía inclinado de otras maneras.

blocks.en: Twisting God's law. Jesus quoted Isaiah against the Pharisees: "This people honors Me with their lips, but their heart is far from Me" (Mark 7:6). The law said to honor father and mother, which included caring for them in old age. But some declared their money corban, dedicated to God, so that they did not have to support their parents (Mark 7:11–13). They tithed their mint and cumin but neglected "the weightier matters of the law: justice and mercy and faith" (Matthew 23:23). They cleaned the outside of the cup and left the inside filthy.
blocks.es_reference: Torcer la ley de Dios. Jesús citó a Isaías contra los fariseos: "Este pueblo de labios me honra, mas su corazón está lejos de mí" (Marcos 7:6). La ley decía honrar al padre y a la madre, lo cual incluía cuidarlos en la vejez. Pero algunos declaraban su dinero corbán, dedicado a Dios, para no tener que sostener a sus padres (Marcos 7:11–13). Diezmaban la menta y el comino pero dejaban "lo más importante de la ley: la justicia, la misericordia y la fe" (Mateo 23:23). Limpiaban lo de fuera del vaso y dejaban sucio lo de dentro.

blocks.en: Robbing God of His glory. God says, "I am the LORD, that is My name; and My glory I will not give to another" (Isaiah 42:8). Some leaders gave and prayed in public "that they may be seen by men" (Matthew 6:1–5), and they "loved the praise of men more than the praise of God" (John 12:43). When King Nebuchadnezzar boasted of the great Babylon he had built by his own power, God humbled him until he lived like an animal in the field (Daniel 4:30–33). Ananias and Sapphira lied to the Holy Spirit to gain a reputation for generosity, and they died (Acts 5:1–11). Taking credit for what God has done is a serious misalignment.
blocks.es_reference: Robar a Dios Su gloria. Dios dice: "Yo Jehová; este es mi nombre; y a otro no daré mi gloria" (Isaías 42:8). Algunos líderes daban y oraban en público "para ser vistos de los hombres" (Mateo 6:1–5), y "amaban más la gloria de los hombres que la gloria de Dios" (Juan 12:43). Cuando el rey Nabucodonosor se jactó de la gran Babilonia que había edificado con su propio poder, Dios lo humilló hasta que vivió como un animal del campo (Daniel 4:30–33). Ananías y Safira mintieron al Espíritu Santo para ganar fama de generosos, y murieron (Hechos 5:1–11). Tomar el crédito de lo que Dios ha hecho es una desviación grave.

blocks.en: God's glory is not a small thing to be borrowed. When Moses boldly prayed, "Please, show me Your glory," God hid him in the cleft of a rock and allowed him to see only His back, because no one could see His face and live (Exodus 33:18–23). If Moses could not look directly on that glory, how dare we try to wear it? This temptation is especially strong for those in ministry. When a church grows, a sermon moves people, or a ministry prospers, the leader is tempted to accept the praise that belongs to God. Every pastor must learn to say with John the Baptist, "He must increase, but I must decrease" (John 3:30). We are ushers who point to the throne, not occupants who sit on it.
blocks.es_reference: La gloria de Dios no es algo pequeño que se pueda tomar prestado. Cuando Moisés oró con valentía: "Te ruego que me muestres tu gloria", Dios lo puso en una hendidura de la peña y le permitió ver solo Sus espaldas, porque nadie podía ver Su rostro y vivir (Éxodo 33:18–23). Si Moisés no pudo mirar directamente esa gloria, ¿cómo nos atrevemos a intentar vestirnos con ella? Esta tentación es especialmente fuerte para los que están en el ministerio. Cuando una iglesia crece, un sermón conmueve a la gente o un ministerio prospera, el líder es tentado a aceptar la alabanza que le pertenece a Dios. Todo pastor debe aprender a decir con Juan el Bautista: "Es necesario que él crezca, pero que yo mengüe" (Juan 3:30). Somos ujieres que señalan hacia el trono, no ocupantes que se sientan en él.

blocks.en: Jesus warned that a house built on sand will fall when the storm comes (Matthew 7:26–27). In AD 70 the Romans destroyed Jerusalem and its temple, and the temple has never been rebuilt.
blocks.es_reference: Jesús advirtió que la casa edificada sobre la arena caería cuando llegara la tormenta (Mateo 7:26–27). En el año 70 d. C. los romanos destruyeron Jerusalén y su templo, y el templo nunca ha sido reconstruido.

blocks.en: The church has faced the same test. In 1517 Martin Luther was horrified that Johann Tetzel was selling indulgences, promising that money could shorten the time of departed relatives in purgatory. Luther's Ninety-Five Theses held the plumb line of Scripture beside the church of his day and found it leaning toward greed that exploited the poor.
blocks.es_reference: La iglesia ha enfrentado la misma prueba. En 1517 Martín Lutero se horrorizó de que Juan Tetzel vendiera indulgencias, prometiendo que el dinero podía acortar el tiempo de los parientes difuntos en el purgatorio. Las Noventa y Cinco Tesis de Lutero pusieron la plomada de la Escritura junto a la iglesia de su tiempo y la hallaron inclinada hacia una avaricia que explotaba a los pobres.

blocks.en: 3. The Church Today
blocks.es_reference: 3. La iglesia hoy

blocks.en: Lukewarm faith. Jesus told the church in Laodicea, "because you are lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I will vomit you out of My mouth" (Revelation 3:16). They thought they were rich and needed nothing, but they were spiritually poor and blind.
blocks.es_reference: Fe tibia. Jesús dijo a la iglesia de Laodicea: "por cuanto eres tibio, y no frío ni caliente, te vomitaré de mi boca" (Apocalipsis 3:16). Pensaban que eran ricos y que de nada tenían necesidad, pero eran espiritualmente pobres y ciegos.

blocks.en: Judging by externals. Peter saw a vision of unclean animals and heard, "What God has cleansed you must not call common" (Acts 10:15). Soon he was preaching in the home of the Gentile Cornelius, and he confessed, "In truth I perceive that God shows no partiality" (Acts 10:34). James warns churches not to give the best seat to the rich visitor and a place on the floor to the poor one (James 2:1–4). It does not matter whether a person is Black or white, rich or poor, educated or not. No church member is more important than another because he can put more money in the offering. Jesus said the widow who gave two small coins gave more than all the rest (Mark 12:41–44).
blocks.es_reference: Juzgar por lo externo. Pedro vio una visión de animales inmundos y oyó: "Lo que Dios limpió, no lo llames tú común" (Hechos 10:15). Pronto estaba predicando en la casa del gentil Cornelio, y confesó: "En verdad comprendo que Dios no hace acepción de personas" (Hechos 10:34). Santiago advierte a las iglesias que no den el mejor asiento al visitante rico y un lugar en el suelo al pobre (Santiago 2:1–4). No importa si una persona es negra o blanca, rica o pobre, educada o no. Ningún miembro de la iglesia es más importante que otro porque pueda poner más dinero en la ofrenda. Jesús dijo que la viuda que dio dos blancas dio más que todos los demás (Marcos 12:41–44).

blocks.en: Worship centered on us. Isaiah's words still apply: people can draw near with their mouths while their hearts are far away (Isaiah 29:13). Worship does not need to be dull, but its spotlight must always fall on Jesus, not on the performers, the building, or ourselves. For roughly the first two centuries, Christians met mostly in homes, not in special church buildings. When Jesus told the rich young ruler what to do with his wealth, He did not say, "Give it to the temple." He said, "Sell all that you have and distribute to the poor" (Luke 18:22). Rick Warren opened The Purpose Driven Life with the words "It's not about you," pointing to Colossians 1:16: all things were created through Christ and for Him. The worship leader Matt Redman wrote his song "The Heart of Worship" after his church in England set aside its band and sound system for a season, so that the people would learn again that worship is about Jesus and not about the music.
blocks.es_reference: Una adoración centrada en nosotros. Las palabras de Isaías todavía se aplican: la gente puede acercarse con la boca mientras su corazón está lejos (Isaías 29:13). La adoración no tiene que ser aburrida, pero el reflector siempre debe caer sobre Jesús, no sobre los que tocan, el edificio o nosotros mismos. Durante aproximadamente los dos primeros siglos, los cristianos se reunían mayormente en casas, no en edificios especiales. Cuando Jesús le dijo al joven rico qué hacer con su riqueza, no dijo: "Dala al templo". Dijo: "Vende todo lo que tienes, y dalo a los pobres" (Lucas 18:22). Rick Warren abrió Una vida con propósito con las palabras "No se trata de ti", señalando a Colosenses 1:16: todo fue creado por medio de Cristo y para Él. El líder de adoración Matt Redman escribió su canción "The Heart of Worship" después de que su iglesia en Inglaterra dejó a un lado la banda y el equipo de sonido por una temporada, para que el pueblo aprendiera de nuevo que la adoración se trata de Jesús y no de la música.

blocks.en: V. The Warning and the Hope
blocks.es_reference: V. La advertencia y la esperanza

blocks.en: "I will not pass by them anymore" (Amos 7:8). As we saw in the Song of the Vineyard, God's patience is great but not endless. Elijah's mantle passed to Elisha (2 Kings 2:13); God's work goes on, but it can pass from careless hands to faithful ones. Jesus warned the leaders of His day that the kingdom would be taken from them and given to a people who bear its fruit (Matthew 21:43).
blocks.es_reference: "No lo toleraré más" (Amós 7:8). Como vimos en el Canto de la Viña, la paciencia de Dios es grande pero no interminable. El manto de Elías pasó a Eliseo (2 Reyes 2:13); la obra de Dios continúa, pero puede pasar de manos descuidadas a manos fieles. Jesús advirtió a los líderes de Su tiempo que el reino les sería quitado y dado a gente que produjera sus frutos (Mateo 21:43).

blocks.en: Yet Amos does not end in ruin. His last chapter promises, "On that day I will raise up the tabernacle of David, which has fallen down, and repair its damages" (Amos 9:11). At the Jerusalem council, James quoted this promise to show that God was now gathering the Gentiles into His people (Acts 15:15–17). The God who measures crooked walls is also the God who rebuilds fallen ones. The plumb line exposes our sin, but it also shows us exactly where we need His grace.
blocks.es_reference: Sin embargo, Amós no termina en ruinas. Su último capítulo promete: "En aquel día yo levantaré el tabernáculo caído de David, y cerraré sus portillos" (Amós 9:11). En el concilio de Jerusalén, Jacobo citó esta promesa para mostrar que Dios estaba reuniendo ahora a los gentiles en Su pueblo (Hechos 15:15–17). El Dios que mide muros torcidos también es el Dios que reconstruye muros caídos. La plomada expone nuestro pecado, pero también nos muestra exactamente dónde necesitamos Su gracia.

blocks.en: VI. Preaching the Plumb Line
blocks.es_reference: VI. Cómo predicar la Plomada

blocks.en: A simple way to preach Amos 7:7–9 is to hold the plumb line beside three walls: Israel in Amos's day, the religious leaders in Jesus' day, and the church today. Under each, name the specific misalignment and support it with Scripture and a clear illustration. A real plumb line in the pulpit, even a weight on a string, makes the sermon memorable. Close by moving from the plumb line to the Person: Jesus is God's straight standard, and He is also the Savior who straightens crooked lives.
blocks.es_reference: Una manera sencilla de predicar Amós 7:7–9 es poner la plomada junto a tres muros: Israel en los días de Amós, los líderes religiosos en los días de Jesús y la iglesia hoy. Bajo cada uno, nombre la desviación específica y apóyela con la Escritura y una ilustración clara. Una plomada real en el púlpito, aunque sea una pesa en un hilo, hace memorable el sermón. Concluya pasando de la plomada a la Persona: Jesús es la norma recta de Dios, y también es el Salvador que endereza las vidas torcidas.

blocks.en: Closing
blocks.es_reference: Conclusión

blocks.en: A plumb line cannot be bribed and does not care how beautiful a wall looks. It only tells the truth. Amos saw the Lord standing beside His people with a plumb line in His hand, and the nation that looked so blessed was leaning toward collapse. The same Lord still measures His people. Are we living for God's glory or our own? Are we doing justice, loving mercy, and walking humbly with our God? Let us return to Christ, let Him straighten what is crooked in us, and worship Him in spirit and in truth.
blocks.es_reference: La plomada no se deja sobornar y no le importa cuán hermoso se vea un muro. Solo dice la verdad. Amós vio al Señor de pie junto a Su pueblo con una plomada en la mano, y la nación que parecía tan bendecida estaba inclinada hacia el derrumbe. El mismo Señor todavía mide a Su pueblo. ¿Vivimos para la gloria de Dios o para la nuestra? ¿Hacemos justicia, amamos misericordia y nos humillamos ante nuestro Dios? Volvamos a Cristo, dejemos que Él enderece lo torcido en nosotros, y adorémosle en espíritu y en verdad.

— Dr. Wayne Cook
Chapala Theological Seminary

mc.stem: A plumb line works because:
options: Gravity pulls the weight straight down, revealing whether a wall is straight
It measures the length of a wall
It shows the direction of the wind
mc.why: The tool is simple but it does not lie; it reveals misalignment.

mc.stem: Before God called him, Amos was:
options: A sheepbreeder and a tender of sycamore fruit
mc.why: Amos said, "I was no prophet, nor was I a son of a prophet" (Amos 7:14).

mc.stem: Amos came from Tekoa in Judah but prophesied to:
options: The northern kingdom of Israel under Jeroboam II
mc.why: God sent Amos north around 760 BC, during Jeroboam II's prosperous reign.

mc.stem: Israel in Amos's day is best described as:
options: Prosperous and religious outwardly, but unjust toward the poor
mc.why: The rich had ivory houses while selling the poor for a pair of sandals (Amos 2:6).

mc.stem: In the first two visions (locusts and fire), what happened when Amos prayed?
mc.why: God's announced judgments are real, and He responds to intercession and repentance.

mc.stem: Why does Amos not intercede in the plumb line vision?
options: Amos had stopped caring for Israel
The plumb line simply shows the truth, and God says He will not pass by them anymore
mc.why: A plumb line does not debate; the wall had drifted and the Owner was measuring it.

mc.stem: The basket of summer fruit vision (Amos 8) contains a wordplay between qayits and qets, meaning:
mc.why: Israel was ripe for judgment: the summer fruit signaled the end.

mc.stem: What does this unit say about the Hebrew word 'anak?
options: It appears only here, and some scholars think it means tin or lead
mc.why: Most translations still read "plumb line," and the point is clear either way: God was measuring His people.

mc.stem: In the New Testament, the plumb line becomes a Person because:
options: Christ is the measure of mature faith (Ephesians 4:13)
mc.why: Jesus is not only the One who measures; He is the measure.

mc.stem: "Sacrifices without obedience" is illustrated in this unit by:
options: A friend who tithed on Sunday as if paying for Saturday night
mc.why: God does not accept sacrifice in place of obedience (Amos 5:21–22).

mc.stem: "Let justice run down like water, and righteousness like a mighty stream" is found in:
mc.why: Amos 5:24 is God's call for justice in place of empty ritual.

mc.stem: Micah 6:8 says the LORD requires us:
options: To do justly, love mercy, and walk humbly with God
To keep every tradition of the elders
mc.why: Micah sums up what the plumb line measures in a single verse.

mc.stem: The northern kingdom of Israel fell to Assyria in:
mc.why: Israel ignored the plumb line, and the northern kingdom fell and was scattered.

mc.stem: The practice of declaring money corban (Mark 7:11–13) allowed some to:
mc.why: They kept the letter of the law while breaking its spirit.

mc.stem: Nebuchadnezzar and Ananias and Sapphira are examples of:
mc.why: God says, "My glory I will not give to another" (Isaiah 42:8).

mc.stem: Martin Luther's Ninety-Five Theses (1517) are presented as:
options: Holding the plumb line of Scripture beside the church of his day
An attack on all church buildings
mc.why: Luther protested Tetzel's sale of indulgences that exploited the poor.

mc.stem: Peter's words in Acts 10:34, "God shows no partiality," address which misalignment?
mc.why: James 2:1–4 makes the same point about favoring the rich in church.

mc.stem: Rick Warren's opening line "It's not about you" supports the point that:
options: Worship and life must center on God, not on ourselves
mc.why: Colossians 1:16: all things were created through Christ and for Him.

mc.stem: "I will not pass by them anymore" (Amos 7:8) teaches that:
options: God's patience is great but not endless
The wall would be rebuilt at once
mc.why: As in the Song of the Vineyard, a day comes when patience gives way to judgment.

mc.stem: Amos 9:11, quoted by James in Acts 15, gives hope because:
options: It announces a new plumb line
God promises to raise up the fallen tabernacle of David
It says the temple will never fall
mc.why: The God who measures crooked walls also rebuilds fallen ones, now gathering the Gentiles too.

sa.prompt: Describe Amos and the times in which he prophesied, including the specific injustices he condemned.
sa.model: Amos was a sheepbreeder and tender of sycamore fruit from Tekoa in Judah, sent to northern Israel under Jeroboam II around 760 BC. It was a prosperous time when the rich built ivory houses and the shrines were full. But the rich sold the poor for a pair of sandals, judges took bribes, merchants cheated with false scales, and the wealthy lived in luxury without grieving for the suffering of others.

sa.prompt: Explain the progression of Amos's five visions and why the plumb line vision marks a turning point.
sa.model: In the first two visions, locusts and fire, Amos prayed and the LORD relented. In the third, the Lord stood on a wall with a plumb line and said He would not pass by them anymore, and Amos did not intercede because the plumb line only showed the truth. Then came the basket of summer fruit, meaning the end, and the Lord at the altar. The visions move from judgment averted by prayer to judgment that cannot be delayed.

sa.prompt: Explain how the plumb line image appears elsewhere in Scripture and how it becomes a Person in the New Testament.
sa.model: Isaiah 28:17 says God will make justice the measuring line and righteousness the plummet, and 2 Kings 21:13 warns of stretching over Jerusalem the plummet of the house of Ahab. The plumb line stands for God's unchanging standard. In the New Testament the standard is Christ: Ephesians 4:13 speaks of growing to the measure of the fullness of Christ, so Jesus is both the One who measures and the measure.

sa.prompt: Explain the two misalignments of Israel in Amos's day, including Amos 5:21–24 and Micah 6:8.
sa.model: First, sacrifices without obedience: God hated their feasts and refused their offerings, because the burnt offering pictured complete surrender while their lives showed none, like a person tithing on Sunday to pay for Saturday night. Second, religion without justice: the poor could not get a fair hearing, so God called for justice to run down like water. Micah 6:8 sums it up: do justly, love mercy, and walk humbly with God.

sa.prompt: Explain how the religious leaders of Jesus' day twisted God's law, using corban and Matthew 23:23.
sa.model: Jesus said they honored God with their lips while their heart was far from Him. The law told them to honor father and mother, but they declared money corban, dedicated to God, so they did not have to support aging parents. They tithed mint and cumin but neglected the weightier matters of justice, mercy, and faith. They cleaned the outside of the cup and left the inside filthy.

sa.prompt: Explain what it means to rob God of His glory, using Isaiah 42:8 and at least two biblical examples.
sa.model: God says, "My glory I will not give to another." Robbing God of glory means taking credit or praise for what He has done. Nebuchadnezzar boasted of the Babylon he built by his own power and was humbled to live like an animal. Ananias and Sapphira lied to gain a reputation for generosity and died. Some leaders prayed and gave to be seen by men, loving the praise of men more than God's.

sa.prompt: Describe the three misalignments of the church today that this unit identifies.
sa.model: First, lukewarm faith, like Laodicea, which thought itself rich but was poor and blind. Second, judging by externals: Peter learned that God shows no partiality, and James 2 warns against favoring the rich; the widow's two coins were worth more than large gifts. Third, worship centered on us instead of Jesus, drawing near with the mouth while the heart is far away.

sa.prompt: Explain how Rick Warren and the story behind "The Heart of Worship" illustrate true worship.
sa.model: Rick Warren opened The Purpose Driven Life with "It's not about you," pointing to Colossians 1:16, that all things were created through Christ and for Him. Matt Redman wrote "The Heart of Worship" after his church set aside its band and sound system for a season so that people would learn again that worship is about Jesus, not the music. True worship keeps the spotlight on Jesus.

sa.prompt: Explain both the warning and the hope at the end of this unit, using Amos 7:8 and Amos 9:11.
sa.model: The warning is "I will not pass by them anymore": God's patience is great but not endless. Like Elijah's mantle passing to Elisha, God's work can pass from careless hands to faithful ones. The hope is Amos 9:11, where God promises to raise up the fallen tabernacle of David, which James quoted in Acts 15 about the Gentiles. The God who measures crooked walls also rebuilds fallen ones.

sa.prompt: Outline how a pastor can preach Amos 7:7–9 using the three walls, and how the sermon should close.
sa.model: The pastor holds the plumb line beside three walls: Israel in Amos's day, the religious leaders in Jesus' day, and the church today, naming each misalignment with Scripture and a clear illustration. A real plumb line in the pulpit makes it memorable. The sermon should close by moving from the plumb line to the Person: Jesus is God's straight standard and also the Savior who straightens crooked lives.
